money_at_stake.rationale: No single published dollar total for 'the value of Russia's blocked diesel exports' exists, so the band rests on several converging, independently cited figures rather than one headline number. Scale: pre-crisis Russian diesel and gasoil exports ran 900,000 to 1,000,000 barrels a day, falling to about 580,000 bpd by June 2026 after refinery strikes, and the ban puts up to 36% of Russia's total oil-product export volume at risk. Realized effect: this is not a projection. In Q2 2026 alone, three separately-listed US refiners, Marathon Petroleum, Valero and Phillips 66, posted net income of USD 5.1bn, USD 3.7bn and USD 3.85bn respectively with refining margins more than doubling, and the US diesel crack spread hit a first-ever triple-digit settlement of USD 102.20/bbl on 2026-08-17, about five times its normal USD 20-40/bbl range. The three refiners' reported net income alone sums to roughly USD 12.65bn in one quarter, clearing the USD 10bn/year threshold before counting European, Indian or other Asian refiners, or product tankers, which is why the band is B10_100 rather than B1_10. Not put at GT_100B: that would require directly cited evidence the total effect exceeds USD 100bn a year, which no source here supports, and extrapolating three months of extreme, record margins into a permanent multi-hundred-billion run rate would be exactly the kind of reasoned-but-unsourced number this leg is not allowed to produce.

evidence.claim: Pre-crisis Russian diesel and gasoil exports ran 900,000 to 1,000,000 barrels a day, falling to about 580,000 bpd by June 2026 after refinery strikes; the diesel and gasoil export ban could put up to 36% of Russia's total oil-product export volumes at risk; Russia's total oil export revenue (crude plus products) fell USD 5bn to USD 15.8bn in June 2026.
evidence.source_name: Kyiv School of Economics, Russian Oil Tracker, July 2026
source_excerpt: Russia had previously exported a steady 900,000 to 1 million barrels of diesel and gasoil per day, whereas in June, following strikes on refineries, exports fell to approximately 580,000 barrels per day.
Amid a domestic fuel crisis, Russia banned diesel and gasoil exports in July 2026, potentially putting up to 36% of its total oil product export volumes at risk.

In June 2026, Russian seaborne oil exports increased by 4.7% month on month and 8.7% year-over-year, according to the July edition of the KSE Institute's Russian Oil Tracker. Seaborne crude oil shipments rose by 13.3% to approximately 4.4 million barrels per day. Oil product exports, by contrast, fell by 13.1% to around 1.6 million barrels per day, the lowest level on record. Total crude oil and oil product exports, including pipeline shipments, increased to 7.7 million barrels per day. At the same time, Russia's oil export revenues fell by $5 billion to $15.8 billion.

public_reach.rationale: This occurrence's own thesis is not exposure to the Russian exporters themselves (Rosneft, Lukoil, Gazprom Neft and other state or sanctioned entities are unreachable, same as every prior Russian-sanctions case this repo has appraised) but exposure to whoever fills the gap, and that side is overwhelmingly listed. Three separately-listed NYSE refiners (Marathon Petroleum, Valero, Phillips 66) already booked a combined USD 12.65bn of Q2 2026 net income directly attributed to the shortage. European integrated refiners saw margins rise above USD 60/bbl on the same dynamic. On the logistics side, LR2 product-tanker owners are capturing premium rates on the longer Persian Gulf and India-to-Europe voyages that are replacing the vanished short-haul Baltic-to-Europe Russian trade. Not scored at the top of the range (85+) for two reasons the evidence itself raises: part of the substitute supply runs through Asian national oil companies that are exchange-listed but majority state-owned, so the public-market share of their margin is partial; and a portion of Russia's lost volume is not being transferred to a competitor at all but is simply destroyed demand (drone-driven capacity loss), which is real economic impact with no listed counterparty on the other side of it.

capture_odds.rationale: Stronger footing than most pre-chain appraisals get, because the capture is already realized and reported rather than projected: three refiners' margins more than doubled and their combined net income hit USD 12.65bn in a single quarter, with payout ratios as high as 59%, which is direct evidence the money is sticking as profit rather than being competed away in the near term. That rests on a genuine physical bottleneck (ultra-low-sulfur-diesel-capable hydrocracking and desulfurization capacity is scarce and takes years to build, which is exactly why the shortage has not self-corrected). Not scored higher, because refining margins are a textbook cyclical commodity spike rather than a durable moat: the USD 102.20/bbl crack is explicitly described as the first-ever triple-digit reading, well above the prior all-time record, an extreme that should compress as Russian refining is repaired, new capacity is bid in, or the ban lifts. The picture is also uneven across the chain rather than uniformly favorable: LR2 tanker owners are capturing real premiums on the longer routes, but the shadow-fleet vessels displaced from the old short-haul Russian trade are reported as waiting for Russian refinery recovery rather than exiting the market, which is latent capacity that could re-enter and compress mainstream rates the moment the ban eases.

timing_fit.rationale: The effect is not a forecast: Q2 2026 results already realized it, comfortably inside the window. What keeps this at 'credible inside the window' rather than 85+ is that the occurrence itself, a rolling administrative export ban, carries only near-term dated commitments: the renewed non-producer diesel and gasoline ban runs only to 2027-01-31 (about 5 months past the 2026-08-29 anchor date), the jet fuel ban expires even sooner in November 2026, and producer refineries were permitted to resume exports starting in September under the same decree. All of these dated commitments fall well short of this repo's 2-5 year underwriting horizon. The realized Q2 profit and the still-active near-term ban together support 'credible inside the window' rather than a higher score, since nothing on the record commits the disruption to persist for years rather than months.

notes.text: Verified Nell's occurrence claim independently (Bloomberg 2026-08-29, corroborated by Hydrocarbon Processing, TradingView/Reuters, Moscow Times and TASS coverage of the same decision): the extension to 2026-09-30 for producer diesel exports, non-producer diesel and gasoline to 2027-01-31, and jet fuel to end-November 2026 all check out. This is the rare case where the appraisal moved the occurrence UP from Nell's own read: her card scored public_market_reach at 78; the Q2 2026 realized results at Marathon Petroleum, Valero and Phillips 66 (not yet public when she likely scoped this, and not cited on her card) are direct, dated, and already-realized rather than projected, which is why public_reach and capture_odds both landed above her selection-stage estimate and the appraisal clears PRIME. The chain build's real work is separating three distinct links that share one headline: US Gulf Coast refiners with spare hydrocracking capacity (money-corner candidate), the LR2/long-haul product-tanker owners riding the rerouted trade, and the shadow-fleet vessels whose eventual return to the water is this thesis's main invalidation risk. TASTE-001 and TASTE-002 do not apply: this is not a rare-earth-miner or Taiwan-concentration thesis.
